Wow. Samsung has been leading Apple in the foldable phone market for seven years, and their philosophy has always been to wait until they can do it better than anyone else before making a move—and the iPhone Duo really delivers!

It's clear Apple has thought carefully about what a foldable iPhone should be, and has taken full advantage of every benefit this form factor can offer…

First, let's talk about the fundamentals. Previous reports have said Apple waited until the technology was mature enough to make the screen crease almost invisible, and to ensure the hinge design is durable enough to withstand countless openings and closings. Whether the hinge holds up remains to be seen, but we can already see how much thought has gone into the design.

Then there's the under-display front camera—visible when you need it, almost invisible when you don't.

Apple has also considered the various ways you might hold or set down the phone, and figured out how to make the software best take advantage of those postures.

I can't remember who first said this, but I think it's absolutely right: great design is something others never think of, yet seems obvious in hindsight. The original iPhone is a perfect example. Other smartphones at the time all had physical keyboards and *required* a stylus to operate, but the iPhone let you use your finger, with the keyboard only appearing when needed. Looking back now, of course that's how smartphones should work.

*Yes, the Duo supports Apple Pencil, but it's not required.

For me, the Duo launch event was full of examples like this. Why do we have to specifically select the subject in a photo, then copy it over to another app, instead of just dragging it directly from the original photo? In hindsight, it seems completely obvious.

Or take the camera timer for selfies—why not have the device simply wait until everyone stops moving, then take the photo automatically? Obvious!

And then there are UI features that exist purely for aesthetics, with no practical use whatsoever, like the blur effect when you fold the device shut.

I could go on, but in summary, I had incredibly high expectations for this device, and yet it still amazes me. I'm British, and we usually use "wow" sarcastically—but this time I genuinely, with zero irony, want to use that word right at the top of the article.

This phone isn't actually the best fit for me. For my needs, the iPhone is roughly 50% ultra-thin camera, 49% pocket-sized portable computer, and 1% phone. The iPhone 18 Pro Max would suit me much better. But I have an intense "tech lust" for the iPhone Duo.

Back to the "slight catch" mentioned in the headline. Apple is exceptionally good at product videos that make us feel like we could reach through the screen and touch the device. Apple knows how to create intense desire for something we absolutely shouldn't buy. Even though I'm not the target audience for the iPhone Duo, I really, truly, absolutely want to buy one. What about you?
